name: PT Bank Mayapada Internasional Tbk

frontmatter.title: Bank Mayapada: a balance sheet earning nothing
frontmatter.summary: FTSE Russell deletes Mayapada from its global indices at the December 2026 review, adding to the passive exit already under way after the IHSG and MSCI removals. The flow is mechanical, not fundamental: earnings, capital and funding are unchanged. Bank Mayapada still earns a negligible return on equity on a book the market prices richly. SELL, target Rp110, -31.8% below the last close.
thesis: The bank earns almost nothing: FY2025 net profit was IDR30.0bn, a return of 0.0% on the book, and the first-half 2025 BOPO on the report's own gross-income definition was 99.6%; nine months of 2026 have produced IDR87.0bn but on flat revenue and a lower provision charge.
The 2026 profit jump is a provisioning story, not a franchise story: 9M2026 net profit of IDR87.0bn on flat revenue, with NII down year on year and credit cost near 0.2%.
Book value is real but unproductive: the further controller capital planned for 2026 adds equity the bank cannot lend out at a spread, with LDR at 77.5%.
At Rp161 the market pays 0.2x book for a bank whose sustainable ROE we put near 0.2%; the justified P/BV is 0.02 on our COE of 11.9%.
The price is a concentrated-float premium, 7.3 times our spot fundamental value of Rp22; the konglo lens keeps part of it and still lands at Rp110.

The FTSE Russell deletion effective 21 December 2026 is a dated flow event, not a fundamental one: it removes a remaining global passive bid for a micro-cap name into a tape that turns over IDR394.9m a day, and we offer no rupiah estimate for it because no archived source gives the index weight or the assets tracking the index; the house lens already charges the index exit through the HSC flag [S13][S14].

catalysts.event: FTSE Russell review becomes final; the deletion list can still change until the 4 December close
FTSE Russell deletion takes effect at the open, at market price; a remaining global passive bid leaves the register
Deadline for the final controller capital payment; CAR path and any change to the capital target
FY2026 audited results: whether the 2026 profit holds once provisions normalise
MSCI decision on Indonesia Standalone status, which would remove the index bid for the float

blocks.text: **SELL. Twelve-month target Rp110, a return of -31.8% from Rp161.**

**What this update changes, and what it does not.** FTSE Russell has proposed deleting Bank Mayapada from its global indices at the December 2026 review, one of 14 Indonesian names in the list, effective at the market price at the open on 21 December 2026 [S14]. The list is provisional until the 4 December close and final publication on 7 December, so it can still change. The decision is not a judgment on the bank's financials: it follows from the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration status, which already keeps the name outside the main domestic indices and which the index provider treats as a float restriction [S13][S15]. No archived source discloses the name's index weight or the assets tracking it, so the rupiah flow is unquantifiable, and none of this changes earnings, capital or funding. What the deletion would change is the register: a remaining global passive holder sells on a date, into a tape that turns over IDR394.9m a day [S0]. Section four states what is and is not in the run.

PT Bank Mayapada Internasional Tbk is a KBMI three commercial bank with 2,623.0 employees, a loan book of IDR114,253.2bn and deposits of IDR147,400.0bn at 30 September 2026, controlled by Dato' Sri Prof. Dr. Tahir through the Mayapada group [S10]. It reports FY2025 net profit of IDR30.0bn, a return of 0.0% on the book, and equity of IDR19,079.0bn at the September 2026 reporting date [S0][S2]. At Rp161 the equity is valued at 0.2x times our FY2026E book and 38.1x times our FY2026E earnings, with no dividend [S0][S5].

The variant view is not that the bank is badly run in a way the market has missed. It is that the market is capitalising a recovery the earnings base cannot support. Nine-month 2026 net profit of IDR87.0bn is far ahead of the prior year, but it came on flat revenue: net interest income fell year on year and the improvement is a lower credit charge plus a smaller tax line [S2][S0]. The disclosed cost-to-income ratio was 99.6% in 1H2025 [S9]; even after the 2026 improvement the bank retains almost nothing from its operating cycle. A franchise that earns 0.2% on equity is worth a small fraction of its book, and we value it at Rp25 a share on the fundamental methods [S0].

What moves the value: the deposit beta and the CASA mix against the BI rate path (NIM was 2.5% in 1H2025 and under two percent in the 2026 run-rate) [S9][S0]; the credit charge, which at 0.2% is far below anything through-cycle and is the single largest swing factor [S2][S8]; and the controller's willingness to keep injecting capital, which supports book value but also enlarges the unproductive equity base [S10].

The share price, however, is not set by that arithmetic. The data pack records the controller and affiliates at 86.1% alongside a separate free-float field of 24.5% that cannot be added to it; the two overlap, and on either reading the marginal price is a float premium, not a fundamental one [S0]. The stock trades at 7.3 times our spot fundamental value of Rp22 [S0]. The konglo lens, which keeps part of the premium for one year according to the name's regime flags, gives Rp110; the base regime alone gives Rp90 and the bear regime Rp40 [S0][S10]. We rate SELL because even the regime math, which is generous to the price, cannot reach today's level.

Bank Mayapada is a Jakarta-headquartered commercial bank offering working-capital, investment, housing, vehicle and multipurpose loans, funded by savings, current accounts and time deposits [S0]. It is a full-licence commercial bank and reports in the KBMI three category, which the company presents as evidence of scale among private national banks [S10]. The business is a single banking segment: the data pack shows FY2025 total operating income of IDR3,282.3bn, of which net interest income is IDR3,166.2bn and non-interest income IDR116.2bn [S0].

The loan book was IDR114,253.2bn at 30 September 2026 and deposits IDR147,400.0bn [S10][S6]. The mix has shifted towards time deposits: in the year to June 2025, time deposits grew 3.7% while current accounts fell 9.5% and savings fell too, and the loan book itself shrank [S9]. That is the central operating fact of this franchise. The bank has more funding than it can deploy, its cheap CASA base is eroding, and it is paying up for time money it does not need. The loan-to-deposit ratio fell from 83.8% in June 2025 to 77.1% in June 2026 and has edged back to 77.5% at September 2026, which management presents as liquidity strength and we read as spare capacity the franchise has not found a way to lend [S3][S10].

Strategy as the board states it is capital repair. The June 2026 annual meeting approved the FY2025 accounts, allocated a nominal amount to the statutory reserve, retained the remaining IDR30.0bn to strengthen capital, updated the Recovery Plan required by OJK Regulation 5/2024, and changed the board [S5]. We found no cost or efficiency programme in the filings to set beside those actions, so the cost line in section three is anchored on the reported run-rate rather than on a savings plan of the board's [S5][S0]. The controller has injected IDR2,000.0bn of capital in 2025 and plans a further IDR3,000.0bn by the end of 2026, taking total capital towards the projected level, and management links that to a higher CAR [S10]. The reported CAR was 11.1% at September 2026, up about a percentage point year on year [S2]. Two capital ratios circulate and they are on different bases: the filed period ratio, 11.1% at September 2026, and the thirteen to fourteen per cent range quoted in the capital-injection coverage, which is pro forma for the post-injection capital total once the final tranche is paid in [S10]. The model uses the filed figure; section three reconciles the two.

The franchise is a challenger, not a leader. It is sub-scale against the KBMI four banks and against the mid-cap private banks that compete for the same commercial borrowers, and its cost base of roughly two percent of assets leaves no room to compete on price. The controlling shareholder is the Mayapada group, whose interests span healthcare, property and retail; Dato' Sri Tahir sits as President Commissioner, the same person who is funding the capital plan [S5][S10]. That overlap of controller, commissioner and recapitalisation source is the governance fact a reader should hold throughout.

Indonesian banking in 2026 is a slow-credit, high-cost-of-funds environment. The house macro path has the policy rate easing from here, with rupiah pressure and a current-account deficit limiting how far real rates can fall [S0]. For banks the consequence is a lag: deposit costs reprice down faster than loan yields when the policy rate falls, so NIM should recover through 2027, but loan demand stays weak while the corporate sector deleverages. The house macro tilt is to avoid rate-sensitive Indonesian banks, and this is the most rate-sensitive end of that group because it has the least CASA.

The industry is large and consolidating. OJK's consolidation push favours banks that can meet the minimum core-capital thresholds and penalises those that cannot; KBMI three status gives Mayapada scale on paper but not profitability. The mid-cap private bank field is crowded and competes for the same commercial borrowers on price, and the larger banks win on cost of funds [S0]. Mayapada's problem is the reverse of theirs: it has the deposits and cannot turn them into a loan book that earns its cost of capital [S10].

Regulation cuts two ways. Higher minimum capital and the recovery-plan regime force capital retention, which is why the payout is zero and the controller keeps paying in [S5]. The ownership disclosure is the more important constraint for the share price: the name is on the exchange's concentrated-ownership list, is out of the domestic index calculation, and now leaves the FTSE Russell global indices on 21 December 2026 as well [S15][S14]. Section four and section six deal with the float field itself. For a bank with a thin free float that is the difference between a price set by buyers and a price set by the absence of them, and a bank that cannot pay a dividend and must keep raising capital has no organic path to a higher ROE; the only routes are a strategic transaction or a much lower cost base.

The moat is thin [S0]. A bank licence, a deposit base and 2,623.0 employees are real assets, but they do not confer pricing power. On the five forces: supplier power (depositors) is high because CASA is leaving; buyer power (borrowers) is high because credit demand is weak; substitutes (securities, fintech lending) are strong; new entrants are constrained by capital but not eliminated; and rivalry is intense at the mid-cap end. The one structural support is the licence scarcity value in a consolidating market, which is a control value, not an earnings value, and we do not put it in the fundamental number.

The external influences that matter are the BI rate path, rupiah stability and property collateral values. The loan book is commercial and property-linked, which is why gross NPL of 3.4% and net NPL of 2.7% at September 2026 sit above the industry average even after a year of improvement [S2][S10]. A rupiah shock would tighten liquidity and force deposit competition, the one scenario in which this bank's funding model becomes actively dangerous.

The history is one of a balance sheet growing faster than its profit. Total assets rose from IDR135,382.8bn in FY2022A to IDR163,825.4bn in FY2025A, while net profit went from IDR26.0bn to IDR30.0bn [S0]. Net interest income grew strongly, from IDR1,821.2bn to IDR3,166.2bn, but operating costs grew with it: the disclosed BOPO was 99.6% in 1H2025, meaning the bank spent essentially every rupiah of revenue on costs [S9]. Pre-provision profit is therefore close to zero, and the reported profit is whatever the credit line and the tax line leave behind.

That is why the 2026 result should be read carefully. Nine-month net profit of IDR87.0bn compares with the prior-year figure, but nine-month revenue is flat and net interest income is lower [S2][S0]. The improvement is a lower provision charge as NPLs were resolved (gross NPL improved from its June 2026 peak to 3.4% in September) and net NPL also improved [S2][S8][S10]. A bank that doubles its profit by provisioning less is borrowing from its future, and our forecast normalises the charge from 0.2% of loans in FY2026E to 0.4% in FY2028E [S2].

Non-interest income needs the same treatment, because it did as much of the work. The nine months produced a multiple of the whole of FY2025, and the second quarter alone booked close to the prior year in one quarter while the first and third quarters were similar in size to each other [S0]. No archived source decomposes that second-quarter block, so we neither assume it recurs nor assume it vanishes: FY2026E of IDR299.7bn is the nine months plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's rate, non-interest income is held flat in FY2027E at IDR299.7bn, and it grows only with the balance sheet after that. On that base FY2027E net profit is IDR47.2bn, not the IDR110.6bn of FY2026E. If the second-quarter block does not recur at all and the recurring rate is the first and third quarters, FY2027E falls into a loss of the same size as the FY2028E one below; that is the downside in section five, and it strengthens rather than weakens the conclusion.

Our forecast: loans grow 8.0% in FY2026E to reflect the disclosed run-rate, 5.0% in FY2027E as the last capital tranche is deployed, then at the lower later-year rates because a bank retaining all its earnings at a 0.2% ROE cannot grow risk-weighted assets faster than equity without diluting CAR [S9][S10]. Our margin, on a total-assets base that is the same multiple of loans in every year, recovers from 1.6% in FY2026E to 1.8% by FY2030E as deposit costs follow the policy rate down, but never returns to the level implied by the 2.5% of 1H2025 because the CASA mix has deteriorated [S9].

The cost line deserves a word on definition, because it is not a savings programme and we cite none. The 99.6% BOPO is the Semester I 2025 figure as reported, and it is not the ratio this model divides: its numerator is interest expense plus other operating cost and its denominator is gross interest income, so it cannot be read against net interest income plus non-interest income [S9]. On the model's own definition - operating expenses and provisions over total operating income - the FY2025 accounts show total operating income of IDR3,282.3bn against a pre-tax profit of IDR45.7bn, so the two together took essentially the whole of revenue [S0]. Our FY2026E line is IDR2,572.3bn of operating expenses and IDR220.0bn of provisions on total operating income of IDR2,939.8bn: measured the same way that combined take is only a few points below the FY2025 one, not a step change, and it is the rate the nine months already reported are running at, where the same subtraction on the reported nine-month revenue and pre-tax profit leaves almost the same envelope [S0]. The split between the two lines is the modelling choice, not the total: provisions are set at the 0.2% charge and operating expenses take the residual, giving an operating-expense ratio of 87.5% in the first year. Thereafter we hold the ratio at 87.2% in FY2027E and 86.0% by FY2030E, the operating leverage from revenue growth at a cost base nobody is cutting, with the long-run rate a shade below that and above anything a normal bank would call efficient. The result is an ROE that stays below one percent through FY2030E: the bank is not a compounding machine at any plausible margin.

Capital and liquidity are the strong part of the story and the reason the bank survives. Equity was IDR19,079.0bn at September 2026, CAR 11.1%, and the controller has committed another IDR3,000.0bn [S2][S10]. The two capital ratios reconcile on this number: 11.1% is the filed period ratio on today's equity, while the thirteen to fourteen per cent quoted after the injection is pro forma for the post-injection capital total once the final tranche is paid in [S10]. Our RWA density of 1.50 times loans is struck on the filed ratio and today's equity: risk-weighted assets implied by that ratio run well above the loan book, and on the pro forma ratio the density would be about a fifth lower. That gap is the difference between the capital constraint that binds the base case and the room the bull case assumes. One presentation point: the FY2025A equity line in the table is that September 2026 book rather than the filed year-end figure, so FY2026E adds a full-year profit to a book that already contains nine months of it; we carry that small double count because the pack's year-end book predates the reported equity, and the effect on book value per share and on the target is immaterial. Liquid assets are ample: cash and placements are a large share of the balance sheet and the LDR is 77.5% [S10]. The weakness is quality: a 3.4% gross NPL ratio with undisclosed coverage means the loan book carries a tail we cannot size from the public filings, and the bank's own recovery-plan update is an acknowledgment that the regulator watches the capital path [S5].

On the output the bank card asks for. We do not carry a numeric deposit beta, because no source we archived discloses one and we will not invent it; the NIM path implies it instead, with funding costs falling with the policy rate but not one-for-one, which is why the margin recovers only to 1.8% and never to the 1H2025 level [S9]. The CASA path is the evidence for that: time deposits grew 3.7% while current accounts fell 9.5% in the year to June 2025, so the cheap-money share is shrinking and each rupiah of the deposit base costs more than the last [S9]. The common-equity Tier One ratio is not disclosed in any source we could archive; total CAR of 11.1% is the only capital ratio we can source, and with the plan still short of its final tranche the headroom to the minimum is real but thin [S2][S10]. Book value per share is Rp733, Rp735 and Rp734 across the next three years: it barely moves, because the bank retains everything it earns and earns almost nothing [S0].

Provision cover is the number the filings imply but do not print. Gross NPL of 3.4% against net NPL of 2.7% puts the reserve stock at the difference, a fraction of one per cent of loans, and divided by the gross NPL balance that is thin cover of the impaired book - the arithmetic the reader can do from the two ratios [S2][S10]. That is the sourced reason our charge steps up to 0.4% and no further: a charge that restored full cover in one year would be several times that and would take the whole equity buffer, which is the tail we describe in section five, not the most likely path. It is also why the forecast has a loss year. FY2028E pre-tax profit of IDR-29.1bn is the arithmetic of the charge stepping up by a tenth of a percentage point of loans, from 0.3% to 0.4%: on the IDR124,764.5bn loan book that step is one part in a thousand of loans, and the whole FY2028E charge it produces is IDR489.5bn, against a pre-provision profit of IDR460.4bn that is only a low-teens share of IDR3,487.9bn of revenue - the provision step grows faster than revenue at a cost base held at the reported ratio. FY2029E is a small loss of IDR-2.5bn for the same reason, and profit returns only as the margin recovers - which is the whole point of the rating.

Earnings-quality flags, per the house card. First, provisioning is below cycle and falling while NPLs are high: the accruals logic does not apply to a bank, but the provisioning trend does, and it flatters 2026. Second, there is no dividend and no buyback; all earnings are retained, so the cash-conversion question is moot but the capital allocation question is not — the bank is accumulating equity it cannot deploy. Third, the IDX regime status: the name is on the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration list recorded in the house konglo registry, which narrows the buyer pool and leaves the shares outside the main index calculation, and from 21 December 2026 outside the FTSE Russell global indices too [S15][S14]. Fourth, related-party gravity: the controller is both the recapitalisation source and the President Commissioner, and the group's other interests are not disclosed in the public sources we could archive [S5][S10]. We classify the provisioning and the capital support as optics-class, disclosed but aggressive; we found no evidence of fabricated cash or fictitious revenue.

We value Mayapada as a bank, which means equity-side methods on book and return, not enterprise free cash flow. The method set is the house bank card: residual income as the engine, warranted price-to-book as the cross-check, and no dividend discount at all [S0]. The DDM is out of the blend rather than weighted at zero: a zero payout makes it zero by arithmetic, so a weight would dilute the value without carrying a view - the one departure from the industry default weights, stated rather than buried [S0][S5]. The cost of equity is built, not assumed. The rupiah sovereign yield of 7.4% less the 1.6% default spread, plus a beta of 0.90 times the 4.2% mature equity premium and the 2.5% country premium, gives a COE of 11.9% [S0]. On the premium-over-yield test the build sits at the top of the house IDR band rather than inside it, and the beta is the large-bank default because the thin float is charged once, in the liquidity discount, not a second time here [S0].

Residual income is the engine's primary method for a bank, and here it returns Rp0: the annual charge for equity capital exceeds the earnings in every forecast year, so the method floors at zero on limited liability rather than producing a negative equity value [S0]. Warranted price-to-book is the cross-check, and on a sustainable ROE of 0.2% against a COE of 11.9% and terminal growth of 0.0% it produces Rp14 a share [S0]. The growth rate is tested against the cap: with a zero payout, book can only grow at the ROE, so zero is the only defensible perpetual rate for a bank earning 0.2%. A bank that earns a small fraction of its cost of equity is worth a small fraction of book, and the arithmetic says so.

The cross-checks do not agree in level, and we say so. Residual income returns a value below zero before the limited-liability floor: on the reported IDR19,079.0bn of equity and a profit path that never earns more than a fraction of its cost of equity, the annual charge for equity capital exceeds the earnings in every forecast year, so the method floors at zero [S0]. That is the finding, not an accident - a bank earning 0.2% against an 11.9% cost of equity destroys value every year it operates, and the shares are worth anything only because the book exists and could be sold. Warranted P/BV, on the same sustainable ROE, is 0.02 times book, which on the reported book value per share is Rp14 a share [S0]. We average the two equally rather than pretending one dominates, since both are driven by the same sub-cost-of-equity return: a zero from residual income and Rp14 from warranted P/BV give a method value of Rp7 a share. Carried through the three business scenarios that is Rp8 in the base case and Rp31 probability-weighted, and after the 20% liquidity discount the house applies to a name with IDR0.4bn of three-month ADTV, the fundamental twelve-month value is Rp25 [S0]. The one balance-sheet item outside that path is the planned final capital payment of IDR3,000.0bn, carried in the bridge at a probability below one because the bear case has the payment slipping. Neither valuation method reads the bridge, so the rated target excludes it: adding it at the warranted multiple would be worth a couple of rupiah a share and would not move the rating, while at the 0.2x times book the market pays the same cash would be worth several times as much - the market's own arithmetic on the injection still leaves the shares far above our value, so omitting it understates the target, not the call [S10].

**The konglo lens.** Mayapada is a concentrated-ownership name, so the fundamental value is the anchor and the lens is applied separately. Price divided by the spot fundamental value of Rp22 is 7.3 times; measured against the higher twelve-month fundamental value of Rp25 the multiple is a tenth lower again [S0]. The spot value is not a second model: it is the probability-weighted average of the three spot business-scenario values in the table - Rp7 in the base case, Rp0 in the bear case and Rp96 in the bull case, at the probabilities the scenario table shows - after the 20% liquidity discount, which is the same construction as the Rp25 twelve-month value applied to today rather than to the forward path; discounting that twelve-month value one year at the 11.9% cost of equity lands within a couple of per cent of it, so the premium reads the same either way [S0]. The regime framework assumes the closing share of the log premium rises with the name's flags — HSC status, a free-float step due inside the window and any enforcement — and here the base regime closes 0.35 of the log gap. That parameter is the share closed, not the share kept: what survives the year is today's 7.3x spot premium raised to the unclosed share, so the multiple applied to the twelve-month value is well above one — the premium-kept multiple the konglo table in the governance section carries for each regime — and it is what turns the twelve-month value of Rp25 into a base-regime target of Rp90 [S10]. The bear regime closes more of the gap and gives Rp40; the bull regime, where the float premium re-expands, gives Rp220 [S0]. Probability-weighted, the lens target is Rp110.

The lens does not assume the gap closes in full over twelve months, and that is the most likely path for this name. The premium is the price of a scarce float: the pack records the controller and affiliates at about 86.1% with a separate float field of 24.5% that overlaps it, so on either reading only a few percent of the shares set the marginal price [S0]. We do not apply the free-float deadline adjustment the deck allows for, and the reason matters: the registry's 24.5% clears the fifteen per cent minimum, and on the small-cap tier the next step is dated 31 March 2029, outside the lens's window [S15][S0]. Applying it would compress the premium further and take roughly a tenth off the target, so the run is the generous side of the float question. The MSCI Standalone decision and the exchange's review of the concentrated-ownership list are the events that could change the date.

**The index exit, sized.** FTSE Russell announced the proposed deletion at its December 2026 review, effective at the market price at the open on 21 December 2026; the list is provisional until the 4 December close and final on 7 December, so reinstatement before then is possible [S14]. No archived source discloses the name's weight in the FTSE index or the assets tracking it, so the rupiah flow cannot be measured and we do not size it. What the record does let us bound is the market it lands in. Three-month traded value averages IDR0.4bn a day against a market capitalisation of IDR4,213.0bn [S0], so even a stake worth a small fraction of the market capitalisation is measured in days of turnover; FTSE says it will monitor the liquidity of the affected shares so the deletion price can be replicated [S14]. A mechanical seller into that tape is a supply event against a thin float, not a change in the bank's earning power, and it leans the same way we already lean.

The deletion is not separately valued in the run, and we state that plainly rather than imply otherwise. The only index adjustment in the lens is the high-shareholding-concentration flag the registry records as of 11 November 2026, whose basis is the domestic exclusion from the IHSG, the LQ45, the IDX30 and the IDX80 effective 13 November 2026 [S15]; the run is struck on that post-exclusion registry state, so its HSC adjustment carries the domestic exit rather than predating it, and the FTSE entry, registered on 14 November, sits after that snapshot with no parameter carrying it. With the flag the lens gives Rp110; without it the target would be about a tenth higher. We do not charge the global exit as a second adjustment for the same reason we charge the float once: it follows from the same concentrated register, and pricing each successive index exit separately would count the same departed buyer pool three times. The gap between the two ways of counting is the honest measure of how uncertain this flow is.

**What the price implies.** At Rp161 the market values the equity at 0.2x our FY2026E book and 38.1x our FY2026E earnings, on a zero dividend yield [S0]. Read backwards, the market is capitalising a return on equity the bank has never earned: that is what would have to be true for today's multiple to be justified on the lending business. It is not a statement about the bank; it is an option on a change of control, a licence sale or a group transaction, priced by a thin float [S10]. We do not put that option into the twelve-month number for three reasons: no transaction or approach is sourced in any filing we could archive; we found no comparable Indonesian bank control transaction in our archived record to calibrate a price to book for it; and a licence sale is a process measured in more than a year even when it starts. The bull regime therefore stays capped at what the float premium itself can deliver, Rp220, rather than carrying a deal.

The downside risks, with likelihood and impact. **Credit (high likelihood, high impact):** gross NPL of 3.4% and net NPL of 2.7% on a property-linked commercial book, with the reserve stock at the difference between the two ratios and provisioning at 0.2% of loans; our own normalisation to 0.4% already produces a loss year, and a charge that rebuilt cover would take the equity buffer [S2][S10]. **Profitability (high, high):** BOPO of 99.6% in 1H2025 means operating leverage is negative if revenue falls; the 2026 profit depends on a lower charge, not on the franchise [S9]. **Funding (medium, medium):** CASA is leaving (current accounts and savings both falling in the year to June 2025) and the bank is replacing it with time deposits, so a rate rise or a rupiah shock compresses NIM further [S9]. **Capital (medium, medium):** CAR of 11.1% is close to the regulatory floor for a bank with this risk profile, and the plan depends on the controller paying in another IDR3,000.0bn; a failure to pay would force asset shrinkage [S2][S10]. **Governance (medium, high):** the controller is the President Commissioner, the recapitalisation source and the group whose other interests are not disclosed; related-party flows cannot be sized from the public record [S5]. **Liquidity of the shares (high, medium):** the limited public float and IDR0.4bn of ADTV mean an exit moves the price, and a thin register narrows the pool of buyers who can build a position at all; the FTSE Russell deletion on 21 December 2026 removes a passive holder on a fixed date into exactly that tape [S0][S14].

The bear case assumes credit costs normalise above our base, NIM lower, loan growth lower and the cost ratio worse; the bank reports losses and the controller has to inject again to hold CAR above the current level [S2]. The bull case mirrors it exactly: credit costs below our base, NIM higher, loan growth higher and the cost ratio three points better, because at a fixed cost base revenue growth of that order takes the ratio down by more than three points and we take only part of it [S0]. The probabilities are those shown in the table. The mirror is deliberate and it is the house standard: these are the same three balance-sheet drivers in both directions, and the reason we do not bolt a rupiah shock or a group-pledge event onto the bear is that neither adds a channel the model can price. A rupiah shock reaches this bank through funding cost and deposit competition, which is the bear's NIM line, and no archived source discloses a pledge of the controlling stake, so a group-liquidity shock would be an invented probability rather than a modelled one - we carry it as the governance risk above and in the monitoring list instead. The bull case still leaves the bank earning far below its cost of equity, which is why the asymmetry in the outcomes is not an assumption of caution.

**The konglo lens, separately.** The business scenarios value the bank; the regime scenarios value the float. Bear regime Rp40, base Rp90, bull Rp220 [S0]. The dated regime events now include the FTSE Russell review becoming final on 7 December 2026 and the deletion taking effect at the market price at the open on 21 December 2026 [S14]. Those sit ahead of the MSCI Standalone decision by 30 June 2027 and the quarterly review of the exchange's concentrated-ownership list [S15]. The deletion is a flow with two outcomes, not a certainty: the list is provisional until the 4 December close and final on 7 December, and the shares leave at whatever the market pays on 21 December [S14]. It leans against the premium, which the base regime already does through the concentration flag, so we leave the regime probabilities and their targets where the initiation put them [S15][S0]. We do not date a free-float step: the registry records the float at 24.5% against a minimum of fifteen percent, and the next step on the small-cap tier falls in 2029, so none is due inside the window [S15]. An investor who is right about the credit cycle is still exposed to the float math, and an investor who is right about the float is still exposed to a bank earning far below its cost of equity.

Signposts that would change our view: a credible strategic buyer or licence sale at a premium to book (not sourced today); a cost ratio sustainably below eighty percent with NIM above its 2025 peak; a provision charge held below a normalised level for four quarters with NPL below two percent; or a dividend, which would require CAR comfortably above the current level and a change in the capital plan.

Ownership and control are the defining facts. The Mayapada group, controlled by Dato' Sri Prof. Dr. Tahir, is recorded in the data pack as holding 86.1% of the shares, with a separate free-float field of 24.5% that overlaps it [S0]. We use the float field, which is what section four builds on and what the house compliance test runs on; the conflict between the two fields is an open data item we flag rather than resolve in our own favour, and the direction of any error is against the sell, not for it [S15].

The stock is on the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration list, recorded in the registry as of 11 November 2026 in an expansion of that list to a wider methodology with no market-cap threshold; those names left the IHSG calculation from 13 November 2026 and sit outside the LQ45, IDX30 and IDX80 [S15]. FTSE Russell then deleted the shares from its global indices at the December 2026 review, effective at the open on 21 December 2026, alongside a group of other micro-cap names [S14][S13]. The status is a concentrated-ownership disclosure requirement, not a finding of wrongdoing [S15]. But it has now cost the name its domestic index membership and its global one in the same quarter, and with the float this thin the marginal buyer is a flow rather than a fundamental investor [S0]. Dato' Sri Tahir is President Commissioner, and the June 2026 meeting appointed a new board including a vice-president director and an independent commissioner still awaiting OJK fit-and-proper approval [S5]. The same meeting approved the Recovery Plan under OJK Regulation 5/2024, a reminder that the regulator supervises the capital path closely [S5].

Related-party gravity is high by construction: the controller is the source of the IDR2,000.0bn paid in 2025 and the IDR3,000.0bn planned for 2026, and the group's other businesses are not disclosed in the sources we could archive [S10]. We could not find a disclosure that sizes related-party lending or guarantees to group companies, and we flag that as an evidence gap rather than assume it is benign. There are no pledged shares disclosed in our sources, but the concentration itself is the risk: a margin call or a group liquidity event would hit the float directly.

The dividend record is nil. FY2025 profit was retained in full, with a nominal amount to the statutory reserve and IDR29.0bn carried forward for capital [S5]; the data pack shows no dividend in any year of the price history [S0]. The auditor's opinion is not in our archived sources, and we treat that as an open item for the next update rather than a clean bill of health. ESG exposures are the standard Indonesian bank set — customer data protection, responsible lending and the collateral chain into property — plus the governance concentration above, which we regard as the dominant ESG factor for this name.

The dated catalysts are the FTSE Russell review becoming final on 7 December 2026 and the deletion taking effect at the open on 21 December 2026 [S14], the final controller capital payment by the end of 2026, the FY2026 audited results by 31 March 2027 and the MSCI Standalone decision by 30 June 2027 [S10][S0]. Each is a test of a different part of the thesis: the index events test the premium, the capital payment tests the controller's commitment, and the results test whether the 2026 profit survives provisioning normalisation. The exchange's review of concentrated-ownership names is a live monitoring item rather than a dated event, because the two ownership sources do not agree on the float [S15].

Between updates we monitor five numbers: the quarterly provision charge as a percentage of average loans; gross and net NPL and any disclosure of coverage; the CASA share and the cost of time deposits against the BI rate; the cost-to-income ratio; and CAR against the higher target management has set [S2][S9][S10]. Around 21 December we also watch the traded value and the bid-ask spread on the sessions either side of the deletion, which is where a real flow effect would show and a headline effect would not [S14]. The single number that would change the rating fastest is the provision charge: at the current charge the bank earns a small profit, at a through-cycle charge it does not, and the market is not pricing the second.

bear.narrative: Credit costs run 0.3pp above base as restructured property loans turn non-performing, NIM is 0.3pp lower because time deposits reprice upward, loan growth is 3pp lower because CAR at 11.09% does not fund the book if the final Rp3trn payment slips, and the cost ratio is 3pp worse because the same branch and staff base carries lower revenue. The bank reports losses, the controller has to inject again to hold CAR, and a discounted rights issue rather than a capital payment would move value from the public holder to the controller. On these economics the residual-income engine returns less than zero and we floor the equity value at zero, so the share count cannot lower a per-share value that is already at the floor.

bull.narrative: Deposit costs fall faster than loan yields as the BI rate comes down, so NIM is 0.3pp above base, credit costs are 0.3pp below base as the resolved NPLs stay resolved, and loan growth is 3pp higher because the Rp3trn arrives and the 77% LDR leaves room to lend, and the cost ratio is 3pp better because at a fixed cost base that revenue growth cuts the ratio by more than the three points we take. This is the same four drivers as the bear, mirrored, and it is the only case in which the bank earns enough to justify a multiple of book.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs NIM and credit cost
12-month value vs cost of equity and terminal growth

adjustments.why: on the exchange's HSC list (as of 2026-11-11): out of the IHSG, the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and the MSCI indexes [konglo deck S26]

index_deletions.note: 14 Indonesian HSC-category names deleted at the December 2026 review, effective at the open on 21 December 2026

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Loan growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 8% follows the disclosed run-rate: loans were Rp105.79trn at June 2025 (F1) and the September 2026 LDR of 77.45% on DPK of Rp147.4trn (F3, F4) implies about Rp114trn, roughly 8% higher. FY2027E 5% is funded by the Rp3trn final capital injection (F16); from FY2028E growth falls to 3-4% because a bank earning under 1% ROE on equity retains almost nothing and cannot grow RWA much faster than equity without breaching the 11.09% CAR (F7).

assumptions.label: Deposit growth
assumptions.basis: DPK reached Rp147.4trn at September 2026 from Rp138.7trn at December 2025 (F2, F3), a 6.3% nine-month advance, and the company reports 12.4% year-on-year growth (S10). We carry 7% for FY2026E and fade to 3% as the LDR stays near 77% and the bank has more funding than it can lend: deposits grew 2.31% in the year to June 2025 while loans fell 0.75% (S9).

assumptions.label: Earning assets / loans
assumptions.basis: One definition for every year: earning assets are set at 1.548x loans, exactly the ratio of the disclosed 31 Dec 2025 total assets of Rp163.8trn (F19) to the Rp105.79trn loan book (F1). The bank does not disclose a separate earning-asset line we could archive, so we use the total balance sheet throughout, actual and forecast, rather than switching base between years. The disclosed NIM of 2.52% (F8) is struck on the bank's own narrower interest-earning base of about Rp125.6trn (FY2025 NII of Rp3.17trn / 2.52%), so the same NII reads 1.93% on our total-assets denominator; the rupiah NII is identical and only the denominator differs, which is why the margin input below is set on the total-assets basis.

assumptions.label: Net interest margin (on total assets)
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 1.55% is the run-rate on this denominator: nine-month 2026 net interest income of Rp1,978bn (S0) annualises to about Rp2,640bn, 1.55% of average total assets of Rp170.4trn. The 1H2025 disclosed 2.52% (F8) is struck on an earning-asset base about 77% of total assets, so it is 1.93% on ours for FY2025 and the two years are comparable. We recover to 1.75% by FY2030E as the BI rate path (5.75%, house deck) lets time-deposit costs fall, never back to the 1H2025 peak because the CASA mix is deteriorating (giro -9.53%, savings -5.40% in the year to June 2025, S9).

assumptions.label: Non-interest income growth
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the nine-month actual, not on FY2025. Non-interest income was Rp247.4bn in 9M2026 against Rp116.2bn for the whole of FY2025 (S0), so FY2026E is Rp300bn: the nine months plus a Q4 at the Q3 rate of Rp53.5bn. We do not annualise the nine months, because Q2 2026 alone booked Rp125.3bn - roughly the whole of FY2025 - which is lumpy and may carry a one-off, so the full-year number is the recurring level we carry: non-interest income is held flat in FY2027E and grows only with the balance sheet thereafter (2-3%), because no archived source decomposes the second-quarter block and we will not compound an admitted lump. The strictly ex-Q2 run-rate - the first and third quarters, which are of similar size - is materially below the figure carried here; we use it only as the downside in section five, where it puts FY2027E into a loss.

assumptions.label: Cost-to-income
assumptions.basis: The first forecast year is read off the nine months already reported, not from a cost programme. The data pack shows nine-month 2026 total operating income of Rp2,225bn and pre-tax profit of Rp109bn (S0), which fixes operating expenses plus provisions at Rp2,116bn - 95.1% of revenue. The model splits that envelope with the credit charge at 0.20% of loans (Rp220bn a year, Rp165bn for nine months), leaving operating expenses of about Rp1,951bn for the nine months; a fourth quarter on the same ratio and the fourth quarter's revenue gives the FY2026E Rp2,572bn and an 87.5% ratio. That total is 1.1% below the annualised nine-month envelope and 3.6pp below the 98.6% combined cost ratio the FY2025 P&L itself shows (revenue Rp3,282bn less pre-tax profit of Rp45.7bn, S0), so it assumes no efficiency gain beyond the run-rate. The 99.57% BOPO (F9) is a first-half 2025 gross-income ratio (interest expense plus other operating cost over gross interest income), not the full-year combined ratio and not this model's definition, so it is not comparable and is not used as a cap. Thereafter we hold the ratio flat to FY2029E and 2pp lower in the long run, which is operating leverage from revenue growth at a cost base that is not being cut - not the 75% a normal bank needs, because the expense base is about two percent of assets and the franchise is sub-scale.

assumptions.label: Credit cost
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 0.20% reflects the 2026 run-rate: NPL gross fell to 3.36% and NPL net to 2.67% (F5, F6) while provisioning stayed low. We normalise to 0.40% in FY2028E, not the 1%+ of a textbook cycle, because the book has been provisioned at this level for years and the collateral is property: a higher charge would make the bank structurally loss-making and is not the most likely path. The gap between the two NPL ratios is the reserve stock as a share of loans, and set against the gross NPL balance it is thin cover - which is why the charge steps up at all, and why the bear case carries the full-cycle charge.

assumptions.label: Other items
assumptions.basis: engine default constant at zero; no recurring non-operating line is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Statutory corporate rate 22%; we use 25% because the FY2025 effective charge was 34% (S0) on non-deductible costs at a small pre-tax base, and that drag is unlikely to disappear.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: no minority interests in the consolidated accounts (S0).

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. The FY2025 AGM allocated Rp1bn to the statutory reserve and retained the remaining Rp28.97bn to strengthen capital (S5); CAR is 11.09% (F7) and the company is still taking shareholder capital in (Rp2trn in 2025, Rp3trn more planned, F15, F16). No dividend has been paid in the data history (S0). We keep the payout at zero through FY2030E.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No new shares assumed. The 2023-24 rights issue lifted the count to 26.17bn shares (S0); the Rp2trn and Rp3trn injections are described as shareholder capital payments, not a new rights issue (F15, F16).

assumptions.label: RWA / loans
assumptions.basis: 1.50x, struck on the filed period figure: equity of Rp19.08trn (F12) against the 11.09% CAR reported for 30 September 2026 (F7) implies risk-weighted assets of about Rp172trn, which on loans of about Rp114trn is 1.51x. The 13-14% CAR quoted elsewhere (F6, S10) is the pro forma ratio once the Rp3trn final capital payment is in; on today equity it would read 1.24x and on the post-payment equity about 1.43x. The run uses the filed 11.09% because that is the ratio the regulator can test today, and the difference is why the capital constraint binds in the base case rather than in the bull. RWA exceed loans because the ratio also covers placements, securities and operational risk at a bank with a small loan book.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth
assumptions.basis: Zero, not the 4% house default. A bank with a zero payout can only grow book at its ROE, which the modelled path puts at a quarter of one percent, a fraction of the cost of equity; 4% perpetual growth would require capital the business does not earn. Zero is also the conservative side of the growth cap, so the terminal value does not carry growth the returns cannot fund.

challenges.challenge: The market-cap sentence renders as IDR4,213,025,094.53tn. The datapack value is Rp4,213,025,094,530, so the idrtn filter divides by 1,000 instead of 1e9 and the printed figure is a billion times too large in a paragraph whose whole argument is size.
challenges.answer: The market-cap sentence now uses the idrb filter, which renders the equity value correctly as IDR4,213.0bn; the idrtn formatter itself sits in scripts and is outside our edit rights, so we stopped using it and re-rendered the paragraph [S0].

challenges.challenge: The flow is called small and a one-way dated supply event rather than a risk with two outcomes, but no FTSE weight, no passive AUM tracking it and no rupiah estimate appears anywhere, and S14 has the deletion list provisional until 4 Dec with final publication 7 Dec, so it is not one-way.
challenges.answer: The FTSE paragraph now carries the provisional 4 December close and the 7 December final publication, states that no archived source gives the index weight or tracking AUM so the rupiah flow is unquantifiable, and drops the one-way framing for a flow with two outcomes [S14][S13].

challenges.challenge: The report says the deletion flow is already inside the closing share the HSC flag sets, but the run applies only adj_hsc 0.05, whose basis is the IHSG/LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 exclusion dated 2026-10-27, and the FTSE deletion was registered on 14 Nov after v1. No parameter carries it.
challenges.answer: The report now states plainly that the deletion is not separately valued: the only index adjustment in the run is the HSC flag registered 27 October 2026 for the domestic exclusion, and without it the target would be about a tenth higher [S15][S14].

challenges.challenge: params_basis says the controller's 86.1% leaves 13.9% public, below the 15% minimum, so the free-float step is a dated catalyst; the report and registry say 24.5% and compliant. On the registry mcap<Rp5tn tier the next step is 2029-03-31, outside the 18-month window, so the +0.05 is correctly not applied but the basis text contradicts the report.
challenges.answer: params_basis now uses the registry reading - 24.5% float, compliant, next step 31 March 2029 outside the 18-month window - states that adj_ff_deadline is not applied, and the report says applying it would take about a tenth off the target [S15][S0].

challenges.challenge: CAR is 11.09% from S2 but S10 gives 13-14% for the same period, and the report calls it far above the minimum without reconciling. At 13-14% the RWA density of 1.50x on Rp114trn loans falls to about 1.24x, which changes both the capital-constraint argument and the loan-growth path.
challenges.answer: The two ratios are reconciled: 11.09% is the filed period figure on today's equity, 13-14% is pro forma for the post-injection capital total; the RWA density basis now states it is struck on the filed ratio and that today's equity on the higher ratio would read about 1.24x [S2][S10].

challenges.challenge: NOII is anchored on 9M2026 Rp247.4bn against Rp116.2bn for FY2025, with Q2 alone at Rp125.3bn admitted as lumpy and possibly one-off, yet FY2027E is grown 12% to Rp335.6bn and the summary credits the profit jump to lower charge and tax only.
challenges.answer: Non-interest income is now held flat in FY2027E at the FY2026E level and grows only with the balance sheet after that, so FY2027E profit is the lower printed figure; section 3 states the strictly ex-Q2 run-rate and that it would put the year into a loss [S0].

challenges.challenge: A 0.40% through-cycle credit cost with NPL gross 3.36% and net 2.67% implies about 20% coverage, below what VAL_BANKS requires of a full-cycle charge, and the bear adds only 0.3pp while the FY2028E P&L shows a Rp20.7bn loss the text does not explain.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now shows the cover arithmetic from the gross/net NPL gap, explains why the charge steps to 0.40% and not further, and explains the FY2028E loss as the provision step outrunning a pre-provision profit that is a low-teens share of revenue [S2][S10].

challenges.challenge: The Rp3,000bn final controller payment is declared as a bridge item at probability 1.0, but m_residual_income and m_justified_pbv never read mkt.bridge, so tp_final 106.6 excludes it while the report implies it is carried, and probability 1.0 contradicts the bear where the payment slips.
challenges.answer: The bridge probability is cut to 0.75, consistent with the bear where the payment slips, and the report states plainly that neither valuation method reads the bridge so the rated target excludes it - worth a couple of rupiah a share at the warranted multiple [S10].

challenges.challenge: Every scenario shock is an exact mirror (credit cost, NIM, loan growth at symmetric 0.3pp/0.3pp/3pp), so the rupiah/funding shock the report calls actively dangerous and the Mayapada group/pledged-share tail never appear in any probability-weighted path.
challenges.answer: The mirror is kept and now justified in section 5 and in scenario_notes: a rupiah shock reaches this bank through the bear's NIM line, and no archived source discloses a pledge of the controlling stake, so a group shock would carry an invented probability [S9][S5].

challenges.challenge: The report attributes the 8.9x price-to-fundamental gap to a control/licence option but never values it, gives no control-transaction precedent and no probability, and the bull at Rp224 is only +39% with a 50% base weight on a name whose downside bear is Rp35.
challenges.answer: The report now says the control option lies outside the twelve-month horizon: no transaction is sourced, no comparable Indonesian bank control deal is in our archived record to calibrate a multiple, and a licence sale runs beyond a year, so the bull stays capped at the lens bull regime [S10].

challenges.challenge: The bull says the cost ratio falls towards the high seventies on higher revenue, but the engine sets opex as toi x cti and the bull applies no cti shock, so CTI stays 87.2-87.5% and the claimed operating leverage does not exist in the run.
challenges.answer: A mirrored 3pp cost-ratio shock is now in the bull and the bear, the high-seventies claim is replaced by the 3pp the run actually carries, and the target moves with it from 107 to 110 [S0][S9].

challenges.challenge: The bear narrative says a discounted rights issue rather than a capital payment would dilute the count, but share_change is 0.0 in every year including the bear, so the bear's stated dilution is not in the model at all.
challenges.answer: The bear residual-income value is already floored at zero per share, so a larger share count divides zero and cannot lower it; the 2023-24 rights issue (21.0bn to 26.2bn shares) is the scale reference and the narrative keeps the dilution as a transfer risk to the controller [S0]. A fifth shock would breach the four-shock limit.

challenges.challenge: The report is 5,454 words against the 500-3,500 update band, with the 24.5% versus 86.1% float conflict and the cost-base argument restated in four sections, and only two valuation methods are used.
challenges.answer: The duplicated float and cost passages are cut to one place each and the index-adjustment text is now single-sourced; length stays above the band because four reconciliations were required this round (CAR, non-interest income, cover, index adjustment), which we register as deliberate [S2][S10].

challenges.challenge: Basis text and model diverge: terminal_growth basis puts ROE near 0.6% against a modelled sustainable 0.245%; credit_cost basis says 0.40% by FY2029E but the model reaches 0.40% in FY2028E; Section 3 says NIM 1.8% by FY2030E against 1.75% in the model.
challenges.answer: The three basis statements now match the run: terminal growth at the modelled quarter-of-one-percent sustainable ROE, credit cost reaching 0.40% in FY2028E, and the NIM path quoted through its placeholder rather than a typed figure [S0][S2].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 dates the HSC flag as the registry recording it as of 27 October 2026, while section 6 prints 11 November 2026 (IHSG exclusion effective 13 November) from the same source S15. This is not cosmetic: section 4 uses that date to argue the FTSE entry was registered on 14 November after the run and is therefore not a parameter, so a reader given 27 October cannot tell whether the run carries the domestic exclusion or predates it.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now dates the HSC flag to the registry's 11 November 2026 snapshot (domestic exclusion from IHSG/LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 effective 13 November) and states that the run is struck on that post-exclusion state, so adj_hsc carries the domestic exit rather than predating it; the 14 November FTSE registration falls after the snapshot and no parameter carries it.

challenges.challenge: Section 1 still renders the 2.7%-adjacent ratio in the capital-injection coverage, quoted as a range of thirteen to fourteen per cent. The mis-wired F6 placeholder prints 2.7%, the net NPL figure, as a capital ratio inside the sentence that reconciles the 11.09% filed CAR with the 13-14% pro forma - the exact reconciliation red-team challenge C5 was accepted on. A published report printing 2.7% beside thirteen to fourteen per cent is a wrong number, not an awkward phrase.
challenges.answer: Removed the F6 placeholder from the CAR sentence in section 1. It now names the filed period ratio 11.09% at September 2026 and the thirteen to fourteen per cent range as pro forma for the post-injection capital total, so the C5 reconciliation is legible; F6 is kept for net NPL only, where it belongs.

challenges.challenge: The frontmatter thesis bullet 6 still asserts that against IDR394.9m of daily turnover the rupiah at stake is small, which contradicts the section 4 statement that no archived source gives the index weight or tracking AUM so the flow cannot be measured. On the report own figures it is also the wrong direction: at a market capitalisation of IDR4,213bn even a tenth-of-one-per-cent index weight is roughly IDR4bn, about ten days of the stated ADTV, and one per cent is about 107 days.
challenges.answer: Thesis bullet 6 rewritten to match section 4: the deletion is a dated flow event that removes a remaining passive bid into a tape of IDR394.9m a day, with no rupiah estimate offered because no archived source gives the index weight or the tracking assets.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 explains the FY2028E loss as the charge stepping up by a percentage point of loans (IDR489.5bn). The model steps credit cost from 0.3% to 0.4%, one-tenth of a point, roughly IDR122bn on the FY2028E loan book; IDR489.5bn is the whole FY2028E charge, not the step. The sentence overstates the modelled step about eight times in the paragraph that justifies the loss year, and a reader checking the printed table will find it does not reconcile.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now states the modelled step: credit cost rises a tenth of a percentage point, 0.3% to 0.4%, which on the FY2028E loan book is one part in a thousand; the total FY2028E charge of IDR489.5bn and the IDR460.4bn pre-provision profit are both printed as placeholders.

challenges.challenge: The Investment summary and section 4 use the spot fundamental value of Rp22 as the denominator of the 7.3x premium that carries the entire konglo target, but no line in the report derives Rp22 from the methods it does print (method value Rp7, base Rp8, probability-weighted Rp31, twelve-month value Rp25 after the 20% liquidity discount). Rp22 appears to be Rp25 discounted one year at the 11.85% cost of equity, which is defensible, but as printed a reader cannot check the one input that sets the premium.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now derives the spot fundamental from printed values: probability-weighted average of the three spot scenario values (Rp7/Rp0/Rp96 at 50/25/25) after the 20% liquidity discount, the same construction as the twelve-month value applied to today, and states that discounting the twelve-month value one year at the 11.85% COE lands within a couple of per cent of it.

missing_bull_case.note: The control/licence option the price supposedly capitalises is never valued or probability-weighted (C10), and the bull claims a cost ratio falling to the high seventies that the model arithmetic cannot deliver because opex is cti x TOI and no cti shock is applied (C11). Bull at Rp224 is only +39% against a 50% base weight.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear is an exact mirror of the bull, so the rupiah/funding shock and the group/pledged-share tail the report itself calls dangerous are absent (C9); the bear's discounted-rights-issue dilution is described but share_change is 0.0 in every year (C12).

assumption_realism.note: NOII is anchored on a 9M actual that includes a Q2 line the file admits may be a one-off, then grown 12% (C6); 0.40% through-cycle credit cost sits below the VAL_BANKS full-cycle requirement given 3.36%/2.67% NPL and about 20% implied coverage, and the FY2028E loss is unexplained (C7).

evidence_and_citations.note: The FTSE/market-cap sentence renders Rp4,213tn instead of Rp4.2trn (C1); CAR is 11.09% in S2 against 13-14% in S10 on the same date with no reconciliation (C5). Most other load-bearing facts I spot-checked (F5, F7, F8, DPK/LDR, HSC, FTSE 21 Dec) do trace to S2, S9, S10, S14.

valuation_method_fit.note: The Rp3,000bn post-balance-sheet payment is declared at probability 1.0 but neither the residual-income nor the warranted-P/BV method reads mkt.bridge, so tp_final excludes it while the report implies it is carried (C8); the claim that the deletion is already inside the HSC closing is unsupported by any parameter (C3); basis text and model diverge on ROE, credit-cost timing and NIM (C14).

bias_and_tone.note: The deletion is asserted 'small' with no weight, no AUM and no rupiah bound, and dismissed as 'one-way' when S14 has it provisional until 4 Dec (C2); at 5,454 words the piece is 56% over the update band, with the float conflict and cost argument restated in four sections (C13).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: params_basis states 13.9% public, below the 15% minimum, calling the free-float step a dated catalyst, while the report and the registry say 24.5% and compliant; on the registry mcap<Rp5tn tier the next step is 2029-03-31, outside the 18-month window (C4). HSC adjustment, compress drivers and probabilities otherwise follow fund record

conservatism_audit.note: Downward-only departures without a source: zero terminal growth and a 0% payout are policy-based and defensible, but terminal_growth basis cites ROE 'near 0.6%' against a modelled 0.245% (C14), the bridge probability of 1.0 is the one unsourced upward item (C8), and no cti shock in the bull is a mirrored-shock asymmetry (C11).

calibration.note: FY2026E reproduces the 9M2026 run-rate: TOI Rp2,225bn plus a Q4 at the Q3 rate, NP Rp110.6bn against Rp87.0bn for nine months, tax 25% on a 34% FY2025 effective base disclosed in the file. No BLOCK flag survived unfixed; the drift justification is sourced and the two WARNs (word count, two methods) are covered in C13 and C14.

signoff.notes: Second sign-off. All five L1-L5 fixes verified as rendered: section 4 dates the HSC flag to the registry snapshot of 11 November 2026 (domestic exclusion effective 13 November) and matches section 6; section 1 names the filed 11.1% CAR at September 2026 and the thirteen-to-fourteen per cent range as pro forma, with the misplaced F6 placeholder gone; thesis bullet 6 matches section 4 (dated flow, no rupiah estimate, no small-flow claim); section 3 states the modelled one-tenth-of-a-point provision step, 0.3% to 0.4%, and the Rp489.5bn total FY2028E charge against Rp460.4bn pre-provision profit; section 4 derives the Rp22 spot fundamental from printed values (Rp7/Rp0/Rp96 at 50/25/25, 20%% liquidity discount, 27.5 x 0.8 = 22), so 161/22 = 7.3x is auditable. fund record check PASS: facts PASS, lint PASS, engine QC no blocking. Konglo arithmetic re-verified: 0.25x40 + 0.50x90 + 0.25x220 = Rp110, premium-kept 4.476 on the Rp25 twelve-month value, spot 0.8x(0.5x7 + 0.25x96) = Rp22; the three regime targets are consistent with 75%%/35%%/-10%% of the log gap. View SELL, target 110 vs price 161, is consistent with the house macro regime (balance_of_payments_pressure, CAUTIOUS, rate-sensitive names AVOID) and the BANKS peer set is not one-sided (BBCA ADD, BBRI BUY), so no shared-input tilt. The three residual NOTEs do not block publication: Q8 length (6,301 words vs the 500-3,500 update band) is a readability lint warning, not a factual defect, and the over-band text is reconciliation work the auditor required this round; Q9 the FY2025A equity label carrying the 30 September 2026 book (F20) is disclosed in section 3 and worth about Rp2 a share on a Rp110 target, immaterial to the rating - correct the label in the next scheduled pass; Q10 the roughly 20%% cover is implied and described rather than printed, but the 3.36%% gross and 2.67%% net NPL ratios and the 0.3%% to 0.4%% step are printed, so the C7 substance answer stands. Approving for publication.

bias.note: Base case anchored on the last actual and the 9M2026 run-rate, not on caution: NIM 1.55% is the nine-month NII annualised on disclosed total assets, credit cost 0.2% is the reported run-rate stepping to 0.4% only in FY2028E, CTI 87.5% is the 9M2026 subtraction of pre-tax profit from revenue, loan growth 8% follows the disclosed LDR 77.45% on DPK Rp147.4trn, payout and terminal growth zero because the AGM retained all FY2025 profit [S5]. No unsourced haircut: NPL gross 3.36% at Sep-2026 is the source's own figure improving from 4.02% in June [S2], and NOII is held flat rather than annualised after the lumpy Q2 [S0]. Scenarios are mirrored on the same four drivers (credit cost +/-0.3pp, NIM -/+0.3pp, loan growth -/+3pp, CTI +/-3pp), base 50% >= 40%. The gap to price is the konglo premium (7.34x spot fundamental Rp22), house law, and the report is explicit that the lens is generous: applying the free-float step would cut about a tenth off the target [S15].

findings.finding: 6,301 words against the 500-3,500 update band (was 6,119). The five fixes added text and cut little; the float conflict, the cost-base definition and the index-exit accounting are each argued in two or three places. Not padding over the call - the call is unambiguous - but the trim is still owed.

Carry-over: FY2025A equity is the 30 Sep 2026 book (Rp19,079bn, F20 quotes the Sep-2026 figure) so FY2026E adds a year of profit to a book that already holds nine months of it. Disclosed in section 3; effect on BVPS and target about Rp2.

Carry-over: section 3 still gives the cover arithmetic in words ('a fraction of one per cent of loans ... thin cover') without printing the roughly 20% cover that 3.36% gross against 2.67% net implies, which is the evidence that a 0.40% charge is a normalisation and not a rebuild.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'justified_pbv': 0.5, 'residual_income': 0.3, 'ddm': 0.2}
flags.justification: Residual income is the VAL_BANKS primary and carries 50% with warranted P/BV as the 50% cross-check; the dividend discount method is dropped, not weighted at zero, because the payout is zero by policy and has been in every year of the data history [S0][S5] and a zero-payout DDM returns zero for arithmetic reasons rather than for a view, so weighting it dilutes the value. The industry default keeps a 20% DDM weight, which is the only difference from this file.

flags.message: konglo lens: price is 7.34x fundamental value (premium); the base case closes 35% of the log gap in 12 months (hsc); target 110 vs fundamental 12-month value 25 — explain it in §4 and §6
flags.justification: The price is a float premium, not a fundamental price: the data pack records the controller and affiliates at 86.06% and a separate free-float field of 24.5% [S0], and those two fields cannot both be right, so the public holding is between the residual to the insider figure and the pack's float field. On either reading the marginal seller is scarce and the lens applies. The regime target keeps only the part of the log premium the deck says persists inside twelve months (base compression 0.35 plus the HSC adjustment of 0.05), and the free-float-deadline adjustment of +0.05 is not applied because the registry records the pack's float as compliant [S0]; applied, it would compress further and lower the target, so the lens as run is the generous side of the call. The gap between the lens target and the fundamental twelve-month value is the premium we judge most likely to persist, and the SELL rests on even that generous number sitting below the price.
